sources.title: Login for AWS local development using console credentials
supports: `aws login` needs AWS CLI 2.32.0 or later
Works for root, IAM user, and IAM federation sign-in; IAM Identity Center uses `aws configure sso` instead
Non-root identities need the SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess managed policy
Credentials refresh every 15 minutes; the session lasts up to the principal's session duration, 12 hours at most
Cache lives in ~/.aws/login/cache; `aws logout` deletes it

sources.title: Managing your costs with AWS Budgets
supports: Budget data is updated up to three times a day, typically 8-12 hours apart
A notification can arrive after spending has already passed the threshold

sources.title: AWS Free Tier
supports: New accounts receive USD 100 in credits and can earn up to USD 100 more
A Free plan account closes after 6 months or when credits run out, whichever is first, unless upgraded
Always-free offers apply on both Free and Paid plans
sources.note: The page does not state the account-creation date from which this model applies.

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront pay-as-you-go pricing
supports: Always-free each month: 1 TB data transfer out, 10,000,000 HTTP/HTTPS requests, 2,000,000 CloudFront Function invocations, 2,000,000 KeyValueStore reads
First 1,000 invalidation paths per month are free, then USD 0.005 per path
Origin fetches from AWS origins such as S3 are free of data-transfer charges

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront pricing (flat-rate plans)
supports: Flat-rate plans exist: Free USD 0, Pro USD 15, Business USD 200, Premium USD 1,000 per month
Flat-rate plans cannot be combined with other offers or discounts
sources.note: Which features and origins each plan allows, and CloudFormation/CDK support for selecting a plan, were not verified. The book's examples use pay-as-you-go.

sources.title: AWS Lambda pricing
supports: Free tier: 1,000,000 requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month
Response streaming: first 6 MB per request free, then per GB
sources.note: The page does not say whether the free tier expires.

`cdkd bootstrap` creates cdkd-state-{account}, cdkd-assets-{account}-{region}, and an ECR repository; it creates no IAM roles and no CDKToolkit stack
Without AWS_REGION cdkd uses us-east-1
A CloudFront distribution is waited for only with --full-wait
State is stored at s3://{bucket}/{prefix}/{stack}/{region}/state.json with an S3 conditional-write lock
AWS::CloudFront::Function is provisioned and read back through Cloud Control API, not a dedicated provider
A non-empty bucket without the CDK auto-delete tag makes destroy fail

supports: cdkd describes itself as for dev/test workflows and recommends the AWS CDK CLI for production

supports: Option names and defaults used in book/vite.config.ts
Pages are written as <path>/index.html; internal links end in /index.html
i18n uses a locale-prefixed file tree; ssg.localeSwitcher adds the language switcher
search-index.json is written to the output root; files under assets/ carry a content hash
codeImports enables `<<< @/path{region}` snippet imports

sources.title: vite-plus 1.1.0 (npm tarball, bundled docs, and local CLI)
supports: run.tasks keys: command, cwd, dependsOn, cache
Tasks are cached by default and package.json scripts are not; `cache: false` cannot be overridden from the CLI
A task with `cache: false` receives the caller's full environment
`vp install --frozen-lockfile` runs the pinned package manager with that flag
Bundles vite 8.3.3, vitest 5.0.3, oxlint 1.87.0, oxfmt 0.72.0
`vp check`'s type check does not cover Vue single-file components

sources.title: vize and @vizejs/vite-plugin 0.443.0 (npm tarballs and local CLI)
supports: `@vizejs/vite-plugin` default export is a Vite plugin that compiles Vue single-file components
`vize check` type-checks .vue and .ts files using the tsconfig include list
`vize lint` lints Vue templates; `--preset essential` selects the essential rules
Adding `@vizejs/vite-plugin` to compilerOptions.types lets TypeScript resolve .vue imports without a shim

There is no vite-plus attribute; `vp` is an unrelated package

sources.title: Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin
supports: AWS recommends origin access control over origin access identity
The bucket policy allows the cloudfront.amazonaws.com service principal with an AWS:SourceArn condition naming the distribution
An S3 website endpoint is a custom origin and cannot use OAC
With signing behavior `always`, CloudFront always uses HTTPS to S3

sources.title: Choose between REST APIs and HTTP APIs
supports: HTTP APIs are designed with minimal features so that they can be offered at a lower price
REST API only: AWS WAF, API keys, per-client throttling, request validation, caching, private endpoints, X-Ray tracing, response streaming
HTTP API only: JWT authorizers, automatic deployments

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Local development
supports: Local development runs Workers in workerd through Miniflare, started by wrangler dev or the Cloudflare Vite plugin
Bindings connect to local simulations by default; `remote: true` on a binding sends its operations to the deployed resource
Workers AI has no local simulation: AI models always run remotely

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Local development
supports: `wrangler dev` uses a local-only D1 by default and persists its data across runs
Local and remote data are separate; `--local` targets the local database for `wrangler d1 execute` and `wrangler d1 migrations apply`

sources.title: Restrictions on CloudFront Functions
supports: CloudFront Functions cannot read the request body
The runtime restricts network, file system, environment variable, and timer access
Execution time is limited and reported as compute utilization

sources.title: Quotas for HTTP APIs in API Gateway
supports: Maximum integration timeout is 30 seconds and cannot be increased
Payload size is 10 MB
300 routes per API by default

sources.title: Lambda quotas
supports: Function timeout is at most 900 seconds
Memory is 128 MB to 10,240 MB
Synchronous invocation payload is 6 MB for request and for response
Default concurrent executions quota is 1,000 per Region; new accounts start with a reduced quota
Environment variables total at most 4 KB

sources.title: Amazon S3 API: GetObject
supports: For a missing object S3 returns 404 when the caller has s3:ListBucket and 403 when it does not

sources.title: DynamoDB read consistency
supports: A write that returned HTTP 200 has been durably persisted
Eventually consistent reads are the default, may not reflect a recently completed write, and cost half of strongly consistent reads
ConsistentRead is available on GetItem, Query, and Scan for tables and local secondary indexes, not for global secondary indexes or streams
Global tables have two modes: multi-Region eventual consistency (default, typically replicated within a second) and multi-Region strong consistency (synchronous replication before the write returns)

sources.title: DynamoDB condition expression CLI example
supports: PutItem overwrites an item with the same primary key unless a condition prevents it
attribute_not_exists on a key attribute is true only when no item with that full key exists
A write whose condition evaluates to false is rejected with "The conditional request failed"

sources.title: Paginating table query results in DynamoDB
supports: A Query returns at most 1 MB per call
LastEvaluatedKey becomes the next ExclusiveStartKey; its absence is the only sign that the result set is finished
A non-empty LastEvaluatedKey does not guarantee that more items remain

sources.title: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode
supports: On-demand tables are billed per read and write request, with no throughput charge at zero traffic
One read request unit is one strongly consistent read, or two eventually consistent reads, of an item up to 4 KB; one write request unit is one write of an item up to 1 KB
New on-demand tables sustain up to 4,000 writes and 12,000 reads per second and can be throttled when traffic more than doubles within 30 minutes
A maximum read or write throughput can be configured per on-demand table

sources.title: Constraints in Amazon DynamoDB
supports: Maximum item size is 400 KB
A transaction can contain at most 100 unique items and 4 MB
Sort key values are at most 1024 bytes and partition key values 2048 bytes

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: DynamoDB, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonDynamoDB
The storage price has a USD 0 tier for the first 25 GB-month

sources.title: amazon/dynamodb-local container image tags (Docker Hub)
supports: Tag 3.3.1 exists for amd64 and arm64 and was the image `latest` pointed at

sources.title: Control access to HTTP APIs with JWT authorizers in API Gateway
supports: The authorizer checks signature (RSA-based algorithms only), iss, aud or client_id, exp, nbf, iat, and route scopes; a failure denies the request
client_id is evaluated only when aud is absent
Public keys are cached for up to two hours
Verified claims reach a Lambda integration at requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims
There is no standard way to tell access tokens from ID tokens; requiring scopes on routes is recommended
For Cognito the issuer is https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}

sources.title: Cognito: the redirect and authorization endpoint
supports: /oauth2/authorize accepts response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, scope, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method
Only S256 is supported for PKCE
The redirect URI must be pre-registered and HTTPS, except http://localhost
An implicit grant is described as less secure because it exposes tokens
An authorization code is valid for five minutes
An ID token is returned only when the openid scope is requested

sources.title: Cognito: understanding the access token
supports: Access tokens are signed with RS256 and carry sub, client_id, token_use = access, and scope
sub is the recommended way to identify a user
Access token validity is configurable from 5 minutes to 1 day
Managed login sets a browser cookie valid for one hour; token durations under an hour are discouraged with managed login

sources.title: Cognito: ending user sessions with token revocation
supports: Revoked tokens cannot be used with Cognito API calls, but are still valid to any JWT library that verifies only signature and expiration
Token revocation is enabled by default on new app clients

sources.title: Cognito: the managed login sign-out endpoint
supports: GET /logout with client_id and logout_uri signs the user out of managed login and redirects to an allowed sign-out URL

sources.title: Amazon Cognito pricing
supports: Essentials is the default feature plan for new user pools
Lite and Essentials include 10,000 free MAUs per month per account or organization, and that allowance does not expire
A user counts as a MAU when an identity operation occurs for them in the month
SMS and email are charged separately
sources.note: Whether managed login is available on the Lite plan is not clearly stated on the page.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: Cognito, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonCognito

sources.title: What is Amazon IVS Low-Latency Streaming?
supports: IVS channels can deliver video with latency under 5 seconds; IVS stages under 300 ms
Ingest protocols are RTMP, RTMPS, and SRT
The data plane (ingest and viewing) is global; the control plane (API, channels, stream keys) is regional
Observed latency varies between users with location, network, and the components in the chain

sources.title: What is Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming?
supports: Real-time streaming delivers latency that can be under 300 milliseconds from host to viewer
Up to 12 hosts on a stage; the resource is a stage, not a channel

sources.title: Amazon Interactive Video Service endpoints and quotas
supports: ap-northeast-1 has endpoints for IVS low-latency streaming, real-time streaming, and chat
One stream key per channel, not adjustable
Default quotas per Region: 100 concurrent streams and 15,000 concurrent views
BASIC ingest bitrate: 1.5 Mbps at 480p or less, 3.5 Mbps above 480p; STANDARD and ADVANCED: 8.5 Mbps; ingest resolution up to 1080p
PutMetadata: 1 KB payload, 5 transactions per second per channel
Real-time stages: 12 publishers and 10,000 subscribers per stage by default

sources.title: Amazon IVS Streaming Configuration
supports: Four channel types; STANDARD is the default; BASIC is transmuxed into a single rendition, STANDARD and ADVANCED are transcoded into several
Exceeding the allowed input resolution or bitrate probably disconnects the stream immediately
The RTMPS ingest URL form rtmps://<ingest endpoint>:443/app/<stream key>
Keyframe interval of 2 seconds is recommended; values above 5 seconds are to be avoided; a 2-second interval gives a stream-start latency of roughly 6 to 7 seconds
For the lowest latency the IVS player is required; H.264 video and AAC audio; CBR is recommended

sources.title: Getting started with IVS: Set Up Streaming Software
supports: OBS Studio 30.2 or later has an Amazon IVS service entry that takes the stream key
A stream lasts 48 hours at most; a reconnect starts a new stream
IVS disconnects after 30 seconds without data from the encoder
The FFmpeg example for RTMPS

sources.title: Amazon IVS Pricing
supports: All streams sent to IVS incur video input costs, even if they are not viewed; input is rounded up to the minute, output to the second
Input per hour: Basic 0.20, Standard 2.00, Advanced SD 0.50, Advanced HD 0.85 USD
Output is billed per hour delivered, by resolution (SD up to 480, HD up to 720, Full HD up to 1080) and by where viewers are served from
Japan is in the output group 'Japan, Hong Kong, and South East Asia'
Free tier for new customers, first 12 months: 5 hours of basic input and 100 hours of SD output a month
Real-time streaming is billed per participant hour
sources.note: The page describes no charge for a channel that exists but is not live.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: IVS
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonIVS
The offer contains only input-hour, output-hour, and real-time-hour products; none for an idle channel
sources.note: The offer has no per-Region file; region_index.json lists only aws-other. The usage types prefixed AP- are described in the file as 'Japan, Hong Kong, SEA'.

sources.title: IVS Costs: Low-Latency Streaming
supports: Auto-record to S3 has no IVS charge; S3 storage, the S3 API calls IVS makes, and serving the recordings are charged
As a rule of thumb, on average 50% of a stream is delivered to each viewer

sources.title: AWS::IVS::Channel
supports: The Channel resource does not create a stream key, unlike the CreateChannel API
Properties Type, LatencyMode (default LOW), Authorized, InsecureIngest, RecordingConfigurationArn, and their defaults
Attributes Arn, IngestEndpoint, PlaybackUrl; the playback URL contains the account ID

sources.title: AWS::IVS::StreamKey
supports: Attributes Arn and Value; Value is the stream key itself
Changing ChannelArn replaces the resource

sources.title: IVS API: GetStream
supports: An offline channel is reported as the ChannelNotBroadcasting error (HTTP 404), not as a response

sources.title: IVS API: Stream
supports: Do not rely on the OFFLINE state; the API may not return it
viewerCount of -1 means the request timed out; health is HEALTHY, STARVING, or UNKNOWN

sources.title: IVS API: StopStream
supports: StopStream disconnects the incoming stream; encoders often reconnect, so revoke the stream key to stop it for good

sources.title: IVS API: DeleteChannel
supports: Deleting a channel deletes its stream keys
Deleting a live channel fails with 409 ConflictException; stop the stream and wait for Stream End first

sources.title: Using Amazon EventBridge with IVS Low-Latency Streaming
supports: Events are best effort: they may be missing, hours late, or out of order (Stream Down before Stream Up)
Detail types, event names, and the example payloads used as test fixtures
Each time a channel goes live it gets a new stream_id
Session Ended may arrive before Stream End

sources.title: IVS Player SDK
supports: The IVS player is required for low latency; latency is under five seconds depending on location and settings
Browsers on iOS get normal-latency playback only; a service worker brings iOS Safari to about 6 to 8 seconds
Third-party players can be brought to about 10 seconds

sources.title: Getting Started with the IVS Web Player SDK
supports: The SDK is offered as a script tag and as an npm module; the page names 1.57.0 as the latest
playsinline is required for inline playback on iOS Safari
The WebAssembly binary must be served as application/wasm when self-hosted

sources.title: amazon-ivs-player 1.57.0 (npm tarball)
supports: create() takes wasmWorker and wasmBinary URLs; the files ship under dist/assets
ErrorType.NOT_AVAILABLE with code 404 means the stream does not exist or is offline, 429 that the viewer limit was reached
getLiveLatency() returns the latency from the server to the player in seconds; isLiveLowLatency() and TEXT_METADATA_CUE exist
The package is AWS Content under the AWS Customer Agreement, not an open-source license; peer dependencies are bowser and lodash
sources.note: Read from dist/index.d.ts and package.json of the installed tarball.

sources.title: Embedding Metadata within a Video Stream
supports: Timed metadata is embedded in the video segments, so every viewer receives it at the same point in the stream
PutMetadata works only on a live stream; there is no guarantee when the metadata is inserted
The web player delivers it as TEXT_METADATA_CUE

sources.title: IVS Auto-Record to Amazon S3
supports: Recordings are written under ivs/v1/<account>/<channel>/<date>/<recording id> as HLS media, thumbnails, and JSON metadata
Process a recording only after the Recording End event

sources.title: What Is MediaLive?
supports: MediaLive transforms live video from one format and package into others, for broadcast and streaming delivery

sources.title: MediaLive: Related Services
supports: MediaPackage is a just-in-time video packaging and origination service that can package content encoded by MediaLive

sources.title: AWS Elemental MediaLive Pricing
supports: A running channel is charged whether or not its inputs receive content; push inputs and channels are also charged while idle
Running time is rounded up to the minute above a 10-minute minimum

sources.title: Cloudflare Stream: Stream live video
supports: Ingest over RTMPS or SRT; playback in the Stream Player or any HLS or DASH player
Every live stream is recorded automatically
Priced per 1,000 minutes recorded and per 1,000 minutes delivered, with no separate encoding charge
sources.note: The page gives no latency figures.

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28: IVS resource types (npm tarball)
supports: register-providers.ts registers no provider for any AWS::IVS type, so Channel and StreamKey go through Cloud Control API; AWS::Events::Rule, AWS::Lambda::*, AWS::IAM::*, and AWS::Logs::LogGroup have dedicated providers
The Cloud Control provider stores the resource model returned by a create as the resource's attributes in state
AWS::IVS::StreamKey Value is on cdkd's list of secret-valued attributes
sources.note: Read from the bundled dist of the tarball, which keeps the src/ region markers. No cdkd command was run against AWS, so what state.json holds for a stream key is not observed.

sources.title: Amazon VPC pricing
supports: A NAT gateway is billed per NAT gateway-hour while provisioned and available, plus per GB processed regardless of source or destination; a partial hour is billed as a full hour
Standard data transfer charges apply on top of NAT gateway data processing
Every public IPv4 address is billed by the hour, in use or idle, at the same rate; Elastic IP addresses attached to NAT gateways are named as an example
A Regional NAT gateway is billed per hour for each Availability Zone it is configured in
sources.note: The page renders its regional price tables with JavaScript. The numbers in the book come from the Price List bulk API, not from this page.

sources.title: What is Amazon VPC?
supports: There is no additional charge for using a VPC; some components such as NAT gateways are charged
Private IPv4 addresses are not charged
AWS Free Tier customers get 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage with the EC2 service

sources.title: Subnets for your VPC
supports: The subnet type is determined by its routing: a public subnet has a direct route to an internet gateway, a private subnet does not and needs a NAT device for internet access, an isolated subnet has no routes to destinations outside its VPC
Network ACLs allow or deny traffic at the subnet level

sources.title: Subnet CIDR blocks
supports: A subnet's IPv4 CIDR block is between /28 and /16
The first four addresses and the last address of every subnet are reserved

sources.title: VPC CIDR blocks
supports: A VPC's IPv4 CIDR block is between /16 and /28
Some AWS services use 172.17.0.0/16, so that range is best avoided

sources.title: Route table concepts
supports: The main route table controls routing for every subnet not explicitly associated with another route table
Every route table has a local route for communication within the VPC
A route has a destination CIDR and a target such as an internet gateway

sources.title: Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups
supports: Security groups are stateful: responses to allowed traffic are allowed regardless of the rules in the other direction

sources.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists
supports: Network ACLs are stateless: responses to allowed traffic are not automatically allowed
Network ACL rules are evaluated when traffic enters and leaves the subnet, not as it is routed within a subnet
The default network ACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic
sources.note: The default rules were read on the linked page https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-network-acl.html.

sources.title: Infrastructure security in Amazon VPC
supports: Security groups work at the instance level with allow rules only; network ACLs work at the subnet level with allow and deny rules, evaluated in ascending order
You can secure your instances using only security groups

sources.title: Enable internet access for a VPC using an internet gateway
supports: There is no charge for an internet gateway itself

sources.title: NAT gateway basics
supports: A NAT gateway is created in one Availability Zone and is redundant within that zone
If zones share one NAT gateway and its zone is down, resources in the other zones lose internet access; one NAT gateway per zone avoids this
A public NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and needs an Elastic IP address
sources.note: The Elastic IP requirement was read on https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html.

sources.title: Gateway endpoints
supports: Gateway endpoints exist for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB only, and need no internet gateway or NAT device
There is no additional charge for using gateway endpoints
Creating one adds a route to each selected route table: destination the service's prefix list, target the endpoint
Prefix lists are specific to a Region, so traffic to the service in another Region does not use the endpoint

sources.title: Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint
supports: An interface endpoint creates an endpoint network interface with a private IP address in each chosen subnet, one subnet per Availability Zone
Interface endpoints are billed for hourly usage and for data processing
Private DNS needs DNS hostnames and DNS resolution enabled on the VPC
The endpoint's security group must allow inbound HTTPS from the resources that call it

sources.title: AWS services that integrate with AWS PrivateLink
supports: Service names com.amazonaws.region.ecr.api, ecr.dkr, logs, secretsmanager, ssm, ssmmessages, and ec2messages

sources.title: AWS PrivateLink pricing
supports: An interface endpoint is billed for each hour it stays provisioned in each Availability Zone; a partial hour is billed as a full hour
Data processing is billed per GB regardless of the traffic's source or destination, in tiers over the Region's monthly total
sources.note: The hourly rate is rendered with JavaScript; the book's number comes from the Price List bulk API.

sources.title: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
supports: Properties VpcEndpointType, ServiceName, VpcId, RouteTableIds, SubnetIds, SecurityGroupIds, and PrivateDnsEnabled

sources.title: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC
supports: By default a Lambda function can reach the public internet; attached to a VPC it can reach only what the VPC can
Connecting a function to a public subnet gives it neither internet access nor a public IP address

The execution role needs ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, DescribeNetworkInterfaces, DescribeSubnets, DeleteNetworkInterface, AssignPrivateIpAddresses, and UnassignPrivateIpAddresses on all resources, and the function's code is implicitly granted them too
A new function stays Pending while Lambda creates the Hyperplane ENI, which can take several minutes; functions with the same subnets and security groups share one
After 14 idle days Lambda reclaims unused Hyperplane ENIs and the function becomes Inactive

sources.title: Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)
supports: Fargate tasks on platform version 1.4.0 or later need both ECR endpoints (ecr.api, ecr.dkr) and the S3 gateway endpoint to pull images privately
Fargate tasks that use the awslogs driver in a VPC without an internet gateway need the com.amazonaws.region.logs interface endpoint

sources.title: Fargate task networking
supports: A Fargate task pulls its image over a public IP address in a public subnet, a NAT gateway from a private subnet, or ECR interface endpoints

sources.title: Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager
supports: Systems Manager without internet access uses the ssm, ssmmessages, and ec2messages interface endpoints, and S3 for agent updates
ssmmessages is required for Session Manager

sources.title: Working with a DB instance in a VPC
supports: A VPC for an RDS DB instance needs at least two subnets in two different Availability Zones

sources.title: AWS Availability Zones
supports: Each Region has at least three Availability Zones
An AZ ID such as apne1-az1 is the same physical location in every account; ap-northeast-1 has apne1-az1 to apne1-az4
AWS may restrict new resources in a constrained Availability Zone

sources.title: AZ IDs for your AWS resources
supports: In Asia Pacific (Tokyo), accounts created before November 2025 have Availability Zone names mapped independently per account
`aws ec2 describe-availability-zones` lists the zone names and IDs of an account

sources.title: AWS Fault Isolation Boundaries: Availability Zones
supports: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with separate power, networking, and connectivity inside one Region
Zones in a Region are up to about 100 km apart and designed not to fail together

sources.title: AWS Fault Isolation Boundaries: Regions
supports: Regions are isolated from each other, which limits a service failure to one Region
Resources and data in one Region do not exist in another unless you replicate them

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: EC2, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonEC2: NAT gateway hours and data processing
The offer also lists a Regional NAT gateway at the same hourly and per-GB rate, and regional data transfer at USD 0.01 per GB
sources.note: The file is about 445 MB. NAT gateway prices live in the EC2 offer, not the VPC offer.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: VPC, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonVPC: interface endpoint hours and data processing, public IPv4 address hours
The offer has no SKU for a VPC, subnet, route table, internet gateway, or gateway endpoint

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28 source: provider registry and property coverage
supports: register-providers.ts registers one EC2 provider for AWS::EC2::VPC, Subnet, InternetGateway, EIP, VPCGatewayAttachment, NatGateway, RouteTable, Route, SubnetRouteTableAssociation, SecurityGroup, SecurityGroupIngress, Instance, NetworkAcl, NetworkAclEntry, and SubnetNetworkAclAssociation
AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint is not registered and is not in the unsupported list, so it goes through Cloud Control API
property-coverage.generated.ts lists the properties the EC2 provider writes; a resource using any other property is routed through Cloud Control API
The intrinsic resolver handles Fn::GetAZs
sources.note: Read from the source archive of the v0.296.28 tag. The npm tarball ships bundled JavaScript without the TypeScript sources. No cdkd command was run against AWS.

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: Cross-Stack References
supports: cdkd resolves Fn::ImportValue against the outputs other stacks recorded in its state, and falls back to CloudFormation ListExports when no cdkd stack exports the name
`cdkd destroy` of a stack whose exports are still imported is refused with StackHasActiveImportsError, and there is no flag to force it
cdkd also resolves Fn::GetStackOutput as a weak reference that does not block the producer's destroy; its documentation calls the intrinsic cdkd-specific
Outputs are stored in the state file; state version 9 records which output keys are Export names
sources.note: Read together with docs/stack-outputs.md and src/types/state.ts at the same tag. Not exercised against AWS. CloudFormation's own documentation also lists Fn::GetStackOutput (see cfn-stack-exports); how the two relate was not investigated.

sources.title: Default security groups for your VPCs
supports: Every VPC comes with a default security group, and a resource created without a security group is associated with it
AWS recommends creating security groups for specific resources instead of using the default one

sources.title: Get exported outputs from a deployed CloudFormation stack
supports: Export names must be unique within a Region for each AWS account
After another stack imports an output value, the exporting stack cannot be deleted and the exported value cannot be modified until every import is removed
CloudFormation documents Fn::GetStackOutput for references across accounts or Regions

sources.title: AWS::EC2::Subnet
supports: Updating a subnet's CidrBlock replaces the subnet: a new one is created and the old one deleted

sources.title: Amazon VPCs and ElastiCache security
supports: All node-based ElastiCache clusters are launched in a VPC; ElastiCache Serverless caches can also be configured with a public endpoint that needs no VPC configuration

sources.title: Inference using Converse API
supports: Converse needs bedrock:InvokeModel; ConverseStream needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream
Order of ConverseStream events: messageStart, content block events, messageStop (with stopReason), metadata (usage and metrics)
contentBlockStart is sent for tool use only; a text delta is {contentBlockDelta: {delta: {text}, contentBlockIndex}}
Shape of a Converse response: output.message.content[].text, stopReason, usage, metrics

sources.title: ConverseStream (API reference)
supports: Request fields modelId, messages, system, inferenceConfig.maxTokens
modelId accepts a base model ID or an inference profile ID
Stream members include internalServerException (500), modelStreamErrorException (424), serviceUnavailableException (503), throttlingException (429), validationException (400)

Errors: AccessDeniedException 403, ModelErrorException 424, ModelNotReadyException 429, ModelTimeoutException 408, ResourceNotFoundException 404, ServiceUnavailableException 503, ThrottlingException 429, ValidationException 400
The AWS CLI does not support ConverseStream

sources.title: MessageStopEvent (API reference)
supports: stopReason values: end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens, stop_sequence, guardrail_intervened, content_filtered, malformed_model_output, malformed_tool_use, model_context_window_exceeded

sources.title: Request access to models
supports: Access to many foundation models is enabled by default; there is no per-model request step in commercial Regions
The first invocation of a third-party model starts an AWS Marketplace subscription, which needs aws-marketplace:Subscribe, Unsubscribe, and ViewSubscriptions and can take up to 15 minutes
Anthropic models need a one-time use case form per account or organization before the first call
Amazon models are not sold through AWS Marketplace
After a model is enabled, callers no longer need the Marketplace permissions

sources.title: Route model inference requests across AWS Regions with cross-Region inference
supports: A geographic profile routes within a geography; a global profile routes to any commercial Region
No additional routing cost; the price is that of the Region the profile is called from
CloudTrail logs the request in the source Region with additionalEventData.inferenceRegion

sources.title: Supported Regions and models for inference profiles
supports: Profile IDs and destination Regions are documented on each model's card
GetInferenceProfile lists the destination Regions of a profile as seen from one source Region
Do not infer the destinations from the geographic prefix of the profile ID alone

sources.title: Prerequisites for inference profiles
supports: A policy that names an inference profile must also name the foundation model in each Region associated with it
The bedrock:InferenceProfileArn condition key limits a foundation-model statement to calls made through one profile
The example for a global profile names the model in the source Region and with an empty Region

sources.title: Model card: Amazon Nova 2 Lite
supports: Model ID amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0; profiles jp.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 and global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0
From ap-northeast-1 the model is offered through Geo and Global profiles, not In-Region
jp.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 called from ap-northeast-1 routes to ap-northeast-1 and ap-northeast-3
Supports Converse and response streaming; max output 64K tokens

sources.title: Model card: Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5
supports: On bedrock-runtime the model needs a geo or global inference profile ID; the bare model ID is not supported for on-demand use
jp.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 called from ap-northeast-1 routes to ap-northeast-1 and ap-northeast-3
Billed through AWS Marketplace; EOL no sooner than 2026-10-16

sources.title: Troubleshooting Amazon Bedrock API Error Codes
supports: ThrottlingException (429) means the account quota was exceeded; retry with exponential backoff and jitter, or request a quota increase
ServiceUnavailable (503) is capacity, not the account quota
A missing Anthropic use case form answers 404

sources.title: Quotas for Amazon Bedrock
supports: Model inference is controlled by per-model quotas on token usage
The quotas that apply to an account can be lower than the published defaults; Service Quotas shows the applied values

sources.title: Response streaming for Lambda functions
supports: Streaming is available through function URLs, InvokeWithResponseStream, and API Gateway proxy integrations
A streamed response is not interrupted when the client disconnects, and the full function duration is billed
Node.js managed runtimes support response streaming natively
Streamed payloads can be up to 200 MB; the first 6 MB is not rate limited
Function URLs do not support response streaming for a function in a VPC

sources.title: Writing response streaming-enabled Lambda functions
supports: A streaming handler is wrapped in awslambda.streamifyResponse, a global the Node.js runtime on Lambda provides

sources.title: Control access to Lambda function URLs
supports: AuthType is AWS_IAM or NONE
With AWS_IAM, a caller in the same account needs lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction in an identity policy or in the function's resource-based policy
With NONE, anyone with the URL can invoke the function once the resource-based policy grants public access

sources.title: Stream the integration response for your proxy integrations in API Gateway
supports: Response streaming is supported for REST APIs only, with responseTransferMode STREAM on proxy integrations
Streams run up to 15 minutes; idle timeout is 5 minutes for Regional endpoints
The Lambda function may keep running after the connection closes

sources.title: Restrict access to an AWS Lambda function URL origin
supports: CloudFront origin access control signs requests to a function URL whose AuthType is AWS_IAM
For POST and PUT the client must send the SHA-256 of the body in x-amz-content-sha256

sources.title: AWS Lambda pricing (response streaming)
supports: The first 6 MB streamed per request is free
The page lists no separate charge for function URLs
sources.note: Same page as lambda-pricing, re-read for chapter 17.

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon Bedrock, ap-northeast-1
supports: Nova 2.0 Lite in Tokyo: USD 0.000396 per 1K input tokens, USD 0.003311 per 1K output tokens
Nova 2.0 Lite through the global profile from Tokyo: USD 0.00036 and USD 0.00301 per 1K tokens
sources.note: The offer has a plain row and a `cross-region-global` row. It has no row named for the jp. profile; the chapter applies the plain row to it, following the user guide's statement that the price is that of the calling Region.

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon Bedrock foundation models (Marketplace), ap-northeast-1
supports: Claude Haiku 4.5 in Tokyo, Regional: USD 1.10 per 1M input tokens, USD 5.50 per 1M output tokens

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: Get started
supports: Workers AI always accesses your Cloudflare account to run models and incurs usage charges even in local development
A Worker calls a model as env.AI.run("@cf/...", {...})

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: Bindings
supports: The AI binding is declared in the wrangler configuration and called as env.AI.run(model, options)
`stream: true` returns results as a text/event-stream
sources.note: This page says nothing about local development or charges; that claim rests on cloudflare-workers-ai-quickstart and cloudflare-bindings-per-env.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Supported bindings per development mode
supports: The AI binding has no local simulation; it connects to the remote service during local development

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: Pricing
supports: Billing unit is Neurons: 10,000 per day free, then USD 0.011 per 1,000 Neurons on the Workers Paid plan
LLM prices are also listed per million input and output tokens for each model

sources.title: hono 4.13.13 (published package)
supports: hono/aws-lambda exports streamHandle, which wraps the app in awslambda.streamifyResponse
streamHandle does not cancel the response body when writing to the Lambda response stream fails, so stream.onAbort does not fire there
hono/aws-lambda is marked deprecated in favor of @hono/aws-lambda for v5
streamSSE calls stream.onAbort listeners when the response body is cancelled
sources.note: Read from dist/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.js, dist/helper/streaming/sse.js, and dist/utils/stream.js of the installed package. Not run on Lambda.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime 3.1149.0 (published package)
supports: ConverseStreamCommand returns `stream`, an async iterable of ConverseStreamOutput
An exception message in the event stream is thrown by the iterator as an error named after the exception
The default retry strategy makes up to 3 attempts
sources.note: Read from the type definitions and from @smithy/core 3.35.2 (event-streams getUnmarshalledStream.js, DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS) in the installed packages. No request was sent.
